title: How Google Traced GKE API Timeouts to a Linux Kernel TCP Bug
gist: Google detailed how three interacting bugs — packet reordering in Private Service Connect, Envoy's half-close behavior, and a Linux kernel bug discarding reordered FIN packets — caused intermittent GKE Kubernetes API timeouts that blocked about 800 developers from deploying. Fixes spanned a PSC rollback, proxy-protocol corrections and a kernel patch by Eric Dumazet, though critics note GKE ran an older 6.1 kernel and the fix was a backport of an upstream change.

insights.claim: Three interacting bugs across Google Kubernetes Engine, Private Service Connect and the Linux kernel caused intermittent Kubernetes API connectivity failures that blocked around 800 developers at one GKE customer from deploying to production.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Managed Kubernetes control-plane networking can fail in multi-layer ways that customers cannot diagnose themselves — a reliability risk for GKE-dependent businesses.
insights.locator: Google recently detailed how three interacting bugs

insights.claim: Packet captures showed the GKE control plane answering new TCP connection requests with stale ACK packets belonging to previously closed connections, leaving sockets stuck indefinitely in FIN_WAIT_2.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Stale-connection state bugs surface as generic timeouts, lengthening time-to-resolution for cloud incidents.
insights.locator: Packet captures revealed that the control plane

insights.claim: The GKE API timeouts stemmed from packet reordering in Private Service Connect, Envoy's half-close behavior preventing TCP connections from closing properly, and a Linux kernel bug that discarded certain reordered FIN packets.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Cross-layer failure chains involving proxies like Envoy are a systemic risk in cloud networking stacks.
insights.locator: The investigation identified three interacting causes

insights.claim: Google's Akash Thakur argues most networking cases resolve at one layer, but this one produced the same i/o timeout symptom at every layer, so each layer had a plausible but incomplete explanation.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Single-layer root-cause assumptions mislead incident response in layered cloud systems.
insights.quote: Every layer had a plausible explanation, and every explanation was incomplete.
insights.locator: Thakur describes a complex troubleshooting case

insights.claim: Individually reasonable behaviors across networking, proxies and operating systems can combine into complex infrastructure failures, and packet captures at multiple network layers plus correlation with infrastructure changes were essential to linking the three bugs.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Observability vendors that correlate network captures with rollout events address a real gap.
insights.locator: Thakur highlights how individually reasonable behaviors

insights.claim: Google fixed the GKE issue over several weeks in three steps: rolling back a Private Service Connect change, correcting proxy protocol handling with regression tests, and a Linux kernel patch authored by former Google engineer Eric Dumazet.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Multi-week resolution for a production-blocking incident illustrates dependency on upstream open-source fixes.
insights.locator: The issue was addressed through three coordinated fixes

insights.claim: The kernel fix was merged into Linux 6.9.7 and backported to the 6.6 and 6.1 LTS branches, reaching GKE customers in version 1.33.5 and later.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: GKE customers on versions below 1.33.5 remain exposed to the FIN-handling bug.
insights.locator: The kernel fix was merged into Linux 6.9.7

insights.claim: Google Cloud managing director Rohan Karne framed the incident as the unglamorous reality of mission-critical platform engineering: methodically ruling out obvious suspects and digging into packet captures until finding the kernel root cause.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Signals Google is using incident transparency as a trust-building message for enterprise customers.
insights.locator: Rohan Karne, managing director at Google Cloud

insights.claim: Sidero field CTO Justin Garrison argued the kernel-patch framing was overstated because GKE runs a roughly three-year-old 6.1 kernel and the bug was already fixed upstream, requiring only a backport.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Lagging kernel versions in managed Kubernetes can expose customers to already-fixed upstream bugs — a diligence point for platform choice.
insights.quote: It turns out GKE just runs a kernel from 3 years ago (6.1) and the bug was already fixed upstream and they had to backport it.
insights.locator: Justin Garrison, field CTO at Sidero

insights.claim: CUHK researcher Guangba Yu says the transferable lesson for AIOps and chaos engineering is organizing simultaneous path observations, protocol state and rollout events while distinguishing symptom recovery from state-machine correction, noting the anonymized case gives no population failure rate.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: AIOps tools must correlate protocol state with rollouts, not just symptoms, to be useful in such incidents.
